Quantifiers of the frame theorems (ok_<fn>, delta_<fn>, delta_step, supply_preserved, total_le, <fn>_readable, ro_name, ro_symbol): every fork from Berlin, every message (any caller, any value, static or not, any depth, top level or nested), every gas, every bound and EVERY message runner (EndsL = EthLib's runFrame returns .ok). The only hypotheses are hfork, hsize' (data size < 2^256, harmless), the selector, the start frame At CODE message 0 [] .empty, the run, s.error = none, and Sep for writers. No runner hypothesis, no callee hypothesis, no hypothesis that restates the conclusion.
s.error = none really means success: EthLib's Halted sets error = some .revert for REVERT (Logic/Rules.lean:1261), so reverting runs are excluded, not counted as success.

The start frame is the real one: goodCall_process uses At.startFrame on EthLib's startFrame, and the run is processMessage's own runFrame with processRunner (Seq.lean:108-141).

findings.claim: status.json never_up: 'supply_never_grows: the same along any finite sequence of calls'; supply_statement and README: 'total supply never grows'; inv_calls: the invariant holds along any sequence.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: The frame theorem total_le is strong (any frame of CODE, any runner, nested or not). The sequence theorems are only about the relation Calls C, whose steps are (a) GoodCall: one successful frame of CODE at pc 0, or (b) Untouched: 'forall n, storageAt S' C n = storageAt S C n', which is ASSUMED, not proved, for everything that is not a direct message to the token. The only step linked to EthLib is a top-level processMessage whose code is CODE (process_step, from Paris). Not linked: a transaction to another contract (router, DEX, multisig) that calls the token inside it, which is how most token calls happen; the rollback of an outer frame after a successful inner token call (after a rolled back burn slot 5 goes back UP relative to the inner end state, so that step is neither GoodCall nor Untouched); fee, refund and block level steps; transactions to other accounts. So 'no sequence of calls can grow the supply' is proved for sequences of direct top-level calls plus steps the reader must take on trust. The statement is true in substance (CODE has no CALL, DELEGATECALL or SELFDESTRUCT, so only frames of CODE at C write its storage), but that EVM fact is not proved here. status.json lists the lift hypotheses (code = CODE, no precompile, no value) under assumptions but does not list Untouched, and not_covered does not mention nested calls. Calibration: the QNT, BNB and WETH audit rated the same Calls-model limit minor for QNT (QNT-2); it is major here by the brief's rule (unproved non-local assumption under a headline) and because the status file does not disclose it.
findings.evidence: token-kit/tokens/wbt/WbtVerify/Wbt/Seq.lean:71-83 (def Untouched, inductive Calls with constructor 'other : Untouched C S S' -> ...'), Seq.lean:21-24 doc ('for the other changes it is the assumption of the step'), Seq.lean:197-212 (process_step: only 'processMessage fork message state substate = .ok ended' with hmc : message.code = CODE), NoMint.lean:154-161 (supply_never_grows by induction on Calls; the 'other' case uses hu 5). status.json assumptions item 6 and never_up.
findings.suggested_fix: Prove a transaction-level theorem: for EthLib's processMessage of ANY message (any code), storage of C at the end is reached from the start by GoodCall steps or equals it, using that only frames with currentTarget = C and code CODE write C (needs: C's code is CODE in the state, and an induction over the runner). Until then say in the headline: 'along sequences of direct calls; calls made from inside other contracts and all other state changes are assumed to keep or roll back the storage'.

findings.claim: delta_<fn>, supply_<fn>, total_le hold 'for every successful call'; 'no mint'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Each of them, for the 12 writers and for total_le on every selector, takes hsep : Sep (callKeys message): keccak separation facts quantified over all 2^160 address words (slot 5 is no balance slot, the balance slots of the three call keys are unique, allowance and blacklist slots of the keys are no balance slot and not slot 5, slots 0 and 2 are no balance slot). Sep is never proved and never shown satisfiable for even one concrete call, so there is no closed theorem that says 'this burn lowered slot 5' or 'this run kept D': the Sanity witnesses give real runs but do not touch Sep, and GoodCall (which carries Sep) is never shown inhabited. The hypothesis is the right shape (per key, not global uniqueness, which would be doubtful over 2^160 inputs) and is almost surely true, and it is disclosed. total_le asks for more than it needs (it only needs slot 5 different from the two or three balance, allowance or blacklist slots actually written). Also supply_preserved and inv_calls need Inv in the start state, which is not established for the deployed storage (disclosed).
findings.evidence: token-kit/tokens/wbt/WbtVerify/Wbt/Sep.lean:61-74 (structure Sep), Invariant.lean:846-852 (delta_step ... (hsep : Sep (callKeys message))), NoMint.lean:40-52 (total_le), Seq.lean:60-68 (GoodCall contains 'Sep (callKeys message)'); TokenKit/Evm/Supply.lean:53-57 (NotBal, UniqBal over all x with x.toNat < 2^160). rg for 'Sep.mk' or an instance of Sep in tokens/wbt: none.
findings.suggested_fix: State total_le with only the inequalities it uses. Add one closed corollary per writer of the form 'Sep for the witness call implies the witness end state has slot 5 lower by 1' so the chain Sep -> conclusion is exercised on a real run.

findings.claim: status.json assumptions: 'Gas: the one-counter meter, before Glamsterdam' and 'from Paris for the lift to top-level messages'; README: proofs about the deployed bytecode on chain.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Two gaps between the words and the statements. (1) No theorem has an upper fork bound: all are stated for every fork from Berlin with Meter := Nat. For Glamsterdam and later the real meter is the two-counter one, so the instances at those forks are about a configuration the chain does not run; the status says 'before Glamsterdam' but the reader has to know that the Nat meter is the limit. (2) The lift stops at processMessage called with its DEFAULT meter and held proof ('processMessage fork message state substate = .ok ended'). EthLib's transaction path (processMessageCall, Transactions/Process.lean:337) calls processMessage with first.meter from prepareFirstFrame, which is GasMeter.commit of the meter left after applyAuthorizations (EIP-7702 list), not syntactically the default; nothing in tokens/wbt links goodCall_process or process_step to processMessageCall or to a transaction. The frame theorems hold for any gas, so this is a missing glue lemma, not a wrong result.
findings.evidence: token-kit/tokens/wbt/WbtVerify/Wbt/Seq.lean:108-118 (goodCall_process: hparis, hmc, noValue, noPrecompile, hsize, K, hproc with no meter argument); upstream/EthLib/EthLib/Execution/Evm/Call/MessageCall.lean:282-287 (meter default); upstream/EthLib/EthLib/Execution/Transactions/Process.lean:279-312 and 337. Every theorem head in Invariant.lean, NoMint.lean, Readable.lean: '(hfork : .berlin <= fork)' only.
findings.suggested_fix: Generalise goodCall_process, process_value_fails and process_step over meter and held (the EthLib lemmas they use already are), then state one corollary for processMessageCall. Say 'Berlin up to but not including Glamsterdam' in the headline.

findings.claim: Path and completeness coverage: 131 paths, every function has one success path, name() and symbol() covered.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: As disclosed: for name() and symbol() only Loops.ro_name / ro_symbol (a successful run changes no storage word of any account, no account, adds no log); the returned string is not proved and there is no witness that they succeed. The 95 revert and 14 stuck paths have no witness, and there is no theorem 'every failing run is one of these', so a revert path may be empty; this does not weaken any headline because every headline is about successful runs and ok_<fn> proves the success end state from pc 0 for any run (a wrongly pruned branch would break that proof, so the 169 pruned branches are checked by Lean, not skipped). The three fallbacks are proved to have no successful run rather than left out.

findings.claim: contract_findings in status.json (owner powers, blacklist and pause reach, no mint).
findings.what_is_actually_proved: They match the readable theorems. Things worth telling the owner or users, all read from proved statements: (1) There is no mint in the runtime code; supply can only fall, by burn (owner, from its own balance) and destroyBlackFunds (owner, any blacklisted address, whole balance, no Transfer event, works while paused). Under the invariant destroyBlackFunds cannot fail on the supply check. (2) The owner can blacklist any address with no event at all, then destroy its funds: two silent-or-nearly-silent steps. (3) transferFrom does not test the spender's blacklist flag, and approve / increaseAllowance / decreaseAllowance test neither blacklist nor pause, so a blacklisted address can still act as spender and still set allowances. (4) Only transfer and transferFrom are pausable. (5) status.json says that after renounceOwnership 'no owner function can succeed (the caller would have to be the address 0)'. Precisely: burn requires caller != 0, but blacklistAccount, destroyBlackFunds, pause, unpause, transferOwnership and renounceOwnership only require sender = ownerOf, with no caller != 0 requirement in the proved statements; so their safety after renounce rests on nobody being able to send from address 0, not on a check in the code. (6) burn lowers _totalSupply before it checks the caller's balance (the second check reverts the whole call, so no harm). (7) An address argument with dirty high bits reverts (arg1 = addrArg1 is a proved requirement).
